suspect:marta_solis: Marta Solis sat with her violin case on her lap during questioning. Her bow hand was steady but her left wrist bore a fresh rosin burn.
event:stairwell_fall: Professor Lang fell from the third-floor landing to the stone lobby below. The railing gave way and the stairs were slick with polish.
motive:stolen_composition: The prize-winning sonata submitted under Solis's name was composed by Jan Kovar in 1987. Lang had found the original manuscript in the archive.
suspect:karl_brennan: Karl Brennan waited in the recital hall after the interval was called. His scarf was caught on the stair rail and torn at one end.
suspect:dr_irina_voss: Dr Irina Voss examined the body and noted the time of impact. Her exam report on Solis's submission was due the following morning.
suspect:felix_morel: Felix Morel had visited the archive six times in the preceding month. He claimed he was researching early recordings of the Kovar sonata.
suspect:anna_czerny: Anna Czerny delivered flowers to the recital hall before the evening performance. She left through the loading dock and was not seen again until morning.
suspect:director_pask: Director Pask held the master keycard for all conservatory rooms. He stated he was in his office from eight until the alarm was raised.
suspect:jan_kovar: Jan Kovar taught composition on the second floor for thirty years. His manuscript notebooks are stored in the archive under restricted access.
location:royal_conservatory: The Royal Conservatory occupies a stone building on a cobbled square. The main door locks at ten and the stairwell is unlit after nine.
location:main_stairwell: The main stairwell rises four floors around a central void. The railing on the third-floor landing shows fresh tool marks at two bolt points.
location:practice_room_six: Practice room six is Solis's assigned space on the second floor. The soundproofing muffles all noise from the corridor.
location:recital_hall: The recital hall seats two hundred and faces east. The programme for the evening listed Solis performing the prize sonata.
location:archive_room: The archive room is in the basement behind a coded door. The humidity control runs constantly and the shelves hold manuscripts dating to 1860.
location:faculty_office: The faculty office shares a wall with the stairwell. A window overlooks the landing and was found open by two inches.
location:loading_dock: The loading dock opens onto the alley behind the conservatory. The security camera was offline for maintenance that evening.
location:corridor_landing: The third-floor corridor meets the stairwell at an unlit landing. The overhead lamp was removed for replacement three days prior.
object:manuscript_score: The original Kovar sonata manuscript sits in the archive under call number K-1987-04. The handwriting does not match the submission copy.
object:exam_report: The external exam report compares Solis's submitted score with known Kovar works. Two passages are marked as identical.
object:broken_railing: The stairwell railing broke at two bolt points on the third-floor landing. The bolt threads show fresh file marks.
object:programme_notes: The evening programme credits Solis as composer of the prize sonata. A footnote thanks Director Pask for his support.
object:rosin_smear: A smear of violin rosin was found on the stair rail near the break point. The rosin grade matches the brand Solis uses.
object:key_card_log: The keycard system records all entries to restricted areas. The archive was accessed at 21:47 from a card assigned to the faculty office.
object:recording_disc: A recording disc from 1989 contains a performance of the Kovar sonata. The performer is listed as a student who left the conservatory that year.
object:scarf_fragment: A torn silk scarf was found snagged on the stair rail. The fabric matches one worn by Karl Brennan at the recital.
object:stair_polish: The stairs between the second and third floors carry a fresh coat of polish. The cleaning schedule shows no polish was ordered.
object:visitors_book: The archive visitors book shows six entries by Felix Morel in the past month. His stated purpose each time was research.
object:comparison_folio: A side-by-side comparison of the Kovar manuscript and Solis's submission reveals identical phrasing in movements two and three.
object:ink_analysis: Ink analysis of the submitted score shows two distinct inks. The annotations in the margins are older than the main text.
object:practice_log: The practice room log shows Solis booked room six from seven to nine. The entry after hers is blank.
emotion:brittle_poise: She answered every question about the sonata without hesitation. Her bow hand rested on the case but her knuckles were white.
emotion:sudden_pallor: He lost colour when shown the torn scarf. He said he had not been above the second floor that evening.
emotion:evasive_phrasing: Each answer about the archive visit was technically accurate and offered nothing more. She spoke as if reading from notes.
emotion:practised_calm: The director folded his hands on the desk and did not unfold them. His responses were complete and unrevealing.
emotion:visible_tremor: Kovar's hand shook when the manuscript was placed in front of him. He identified the handwriting as his own without being asked.
emotion:forced_warmth: Morel smiled at every question and offered to help with the investigation. His eyes moved to the archive door twice.
modifier:railing_loosened: Two bolts on the third-floor railing were filed down to half their original diameter. The filing was done with a fine-grade metal file.
modifier:polish_applied: Polish was applied to the stairs between the second and third floors. The application pattern is uneven and concentrated near the landing.
modifier:scarf_snagged: The scarf fragment caught on a bolt head protruding from the loosened railing. The tear is consistent with a downward pull.
modifier:ink_mismatch: The submitted score uses two inks that differ in iron content. The marginal annotations match ink manufactured before 1990.
modifier:corridor_dark: The third-floor corridor has no working lamp. The replacement bulb was ordered but not yet installed.
modifier:door_ajar: Practice room six was found unlocked and ajar at midnight. The soundproofing seal was not engaged.
modifier:rosin_on_rail: Violin rosin was found on the railing surface near the loosened bolts. The residue is consistent with transfer from a player's fingers.
modifier:page_missing: Page seven of the exam report is missing from the faculty office copy. The staple holes show it was removed after binding.
modifier:handwriting_copied: The submitted score imitates Kovar's notation style but the slant differs by four degrees. A trained graphologist would detect the copy.
modifier:fresh_polish: The stair polish had not fully dried when the body was found. Application was estimated at less than two hours before the fall.
action:score_submitted: Solis submitted the prize sonata under her own name four months before the recital. The submission form lists no co-author or source.
action:stair_polished: Polish was applied to the stairwell steps between the second and third floors. No cleaning staff member claims responsibility.
action:archive_visited: The archive was accessed at 21:47 during the recital interval. The keycard used was assigned to the faculty office pool.
action:railing_tampered: Two railing bolts were filed to reduce their load-bearing capacity. The filing was precise and required a specific tool.
action:exam_confronted: Professor Lang confronted Solis about the manuscript during the interval. A witness heard raised voices near the landing.
action:recording_erased: The 1989 recording disc was found with its index entry scratched out. The catalogue card in the archive was also removed.
action:bouquet_delivered: Anna Czerny delivered a bouquet to the recital hall at half past six. She spoke with the stage manager and left via the dock.
action:folio_compared: Lang placed the Kovar manuscript beside the submitted score on his desk. He marked two passages and circled the date on the original.
action:door_locked: Practice room six was locked from the corridor side after the recital. The key was found in the faculty office drawer.
time:recital_interval: The recital interval began at 21:30 and lasted fifteen minutes. The stairwell was accessible from the corridor during this period.
time:evening_rehearsal: The evening rehearsal ran from seven to nine in the recital hall. Solis performed the prize sonata as the final piece.
time:body_found_dawn: The cleaning woman found Professor Lang at the bottom of the stairwell at six. The body had been there for several hours.
time:archive_access: The archive keycard log shows a single entry at 21:47. No exit was logged, suggesting the door was held open.
time:submission_deadline: The prize submission closed four months before the recital. Solis was the only entrant who submitted a full sonata.
motive:prize_ambition: The composition prize carries a stipend and a guaranteed recording contract. Solis had applied twice before without success.
motive:faculty_rivalry: Jan Kovar and Marta Solis competed for the same teaching position. The appointment was pending the outcome of the prize.
motive:plagiarism_exposure: If Lang's exam report reached the committee, Solis would face expulsion. Her previous degree would also be reviewed.
motive:funding_loss: Director Pask had secured funding for the conservatory based on the prize winner's reputation. A plagiarism finding would end the grant.
motive:personal_vendetta: Felix Morel had been romantically involved with Solis the previous year. The relationship ended when she submitted the sonata.
witness:stage_manager: The stage manager heard raised voices near the third-floor landing at 21:35. He did not investigate because of the interval crowd.
witness:piano_tuner: The piano tuner was in the recital hall until ten. He saw no one enter from the stairwell side after the interval.
witness:cleaning_woman: The cleaning woman found the body at six in the morning. She noted the stairs were unusually slippery and the railing was broken.
witness:front_desk: The front desk logged all keycard swipes after nine. Only three cards were used between 21:00 and 22:00.
witness:page_turner: The page turner sat beside Solis during the rehearsal. She said Solis played from memory and never opened the score.
event:professor_lang_discovered: Professor Lang was found at the base of the main stairwell at dawn. His briefcase was open and the exam report was beside him.
event:evening_recital: The evening recital featured four performers and an interval at 21:30. Solis played the prize sonata to a full house.
